metadata.description: A host- or cluster-scoped virtual network that workloads (VMs, pods) attach to — the attachment POINT between guest vNICs and the host L2 stack. Realized by e.g. a libvirt network (forward mode=bridge/nat/routed/isolated), a Kubernetes NetworkAttachmentDefinition (Multus/CNI), or an OVN logical switch — the vendor mechanism is the provider, never the type. Completes graph traversal guest → VirtualNetwork → (references) underlying bridge/uplink Hardware.NetworkInterface → bond → NIC → switch. Consumers declare attachment by binds_to on the consumer side (a VM binds_to its VirtualNetwork), which implies depends_on: the network exists before the guest starts; guests stop before it tears down.

zone.description: WHAT KIND OF NETWORK THIS IS — DMZ, management, internal, storage — as a governed TAXONOMY term (Knowledge.TaxonomyTerm), not a property bundle and not a floor. A CLASSIFICATION, NOT A REQUIREMENT, and the distinction is why this is a taxonomy where `tier` is reference data: a floor is something a second provider can MEET, a category is something a thing IS. Taxonomy is also the only one of the two that carries `normalization_rules`, which is what this needs — providers report `dmz-2`, `DMZ_RESTRICTED` and `dmz restricted`, and all three have to land on one canonical term before any policy can match on it. FOR PLACEMENT ONLY (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10). Nothing critical hangs off a zone directly: it is not an authorization, not a control, and not a boundary. ANYTHING REQUIRED BECAUSE OF A ZONE IS ENFORCED BY POLICY READING IT — the model carries the classification, policy acts on it, which is the same split that governs everything else here. That also keeps the model on the right side of zero-trust architecture, which derives no trust from network location (NIST SP 800-207); UDLM already ships a `zero_trust.posture` setting that a location-as-trust reading would contradict. ON THE BASE though it does not apply to every network type (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10): enough of the family carries a category that the base is the right home, and an element that some types leave unpopulated is what `optional` is for. Scope IS portability (ADR-038 §3) — a category two providers can both report is portable by definition. Provider-reported, like `tier`.

tier.description: HOW GOOD THIS NETWORK IS — a reference to a governed `network_tier`, exactly parallel to `storage_tier`. Each term DENOTES A FLOOR (bandwidth, latency), so asking for a tier is asking for the floor and any network meeting it qualifies: one provider's "10G" and another's "high-throughput" are interchangeable iff both clear it. That is what keeps the intent portable — the match is against the floor, never the string. NAME-SELECTABLE BUT REQUIREMENTS-AUTHORITATIVE (ADR-036, ruled 2026-07-27): a consumer may select by tier name, explicit requirements win where both are given, and the provider records its native class as a realized output rather than something the consumer had to know. ON THE BASE, NOT A TYPE, because performance is expected to be consumable by ALL network class providers and portable (maintainer ruling 2026-08-10). Scope IS portability (ADR-038 §3), so the category base is where a fact every provider must report belongs. Provider-reported at registration or discovery — the party that knows is the one that says.

forward_mode.description: How traffic leaves the virtual network (libvirt forward-mode vocabulary). bridge = transparent onto an underlying host bridge; nat/routed = via the host stack; isolated = no egress.

autostart.description: Network is activated with the host.

location.description: The network's name on its host/cluster (e.g. 'host-bridge', 'default') — unique within the containing scope.

role.description: Semantic usage, e.g. workload | mgmt | test.

attachment_ready.description: Network is active and attachable once Realized (libvirt net-list active analog).

relationships.name: host
relationships.description: The host providing a host-scoped virtual network (libvirt case). Guests stop before the host regardless; this scopes the network's lifecycle to its host.

relationships.name: cluster
relationships.description: Cluster-scoped virtual networks (NetworkAttachmentDefinition / OVN logical networks).

supporting_node (RFC 8345; renamed from underlying_device when relation names were adopted from standards, common-elements §9) — the bridge (or uplink) interface a forward_mode=bridge network forwards onto. The hop that joins the guest-attachment layer to the physical L2 stack (common-elements §7/§7a).

context.purpose: Models the attachment point workloads plug into — the host- or cluster-scoped network a guest names when it says attach me here.
context.plain_description: The network a VM's or pod's NIC attaches to: a libvirt network, a Kubernetes NetworkAttachmentDefinition, an OVN logical switch — whichever; the mechanism is the provider. It declares how traffic leaves — `forward_mode`, in libvirt's vocabulary: `bridge` (straight onto a host bridge), `nat`, `routed`, or `isolated` — and references downward: the VLAN segment it rides and the host bridge or uplink interface supporting it. That downward reference completes the walkable path guest → virtual network → bridge → bond → NIC → switch.
use_when: You need VMs or pods to attach to networks by selecting an existing named network rather than describing L2 details inline.
You need the guest-to-physical-network path traversable for impact analysis — e.g. which guests a bridge change affects.
not_for: The VLAN id or segment itself — Network.VLAN; a virtual network rides a segment, referenced not restated.
The host bridge device — Hardware.NetworkInterface (device_class bridge) supports this network from below.
Per-guest NIC intent — that lives on Compute.VM's own networks list.
works_with: Compute.VM / Compute.Cluster — the guests that attach, and the scope that hosts the network.
Network.VLAN — the underlying segment, selected by reference.
Hardware.NetworkInterface — the supporting bridge or uplink on the host.
Network.IPAddressPool — the address pool scoped to this segment.
